sections.title: Listening. Listen to a radio interview with a crime writer. Choose the correct answers.
sections.script:
Presenter: My guest today is Madina Karimova, who writes detective stories. Madina, where do your ideas come from?
Madina: Mostly from real life. I'm interested in why people commit crimes — not how. Usually they're ordinary people who make one bad decision.
Presenter: Do you meet real criminals?
Madina: Sometimes. I once interviewed a man who had been a pickpocket for twenty years. He told me that everybody thinks they would notice a thief, but nobody does.
Presenter: Were you nervous?
Madina: A little! We met in a café, and he could see my bag on the chair the whole time. I kept my hand on it!
Presenter: Your books are very popular now. Why do you think that is?
Madina: I think it's because the detective is a normal schoolteacher, not a police officer. Readers say she reminds them of someone they know.

The pickpocket told her that

o: the man could see her bag.

sections.title: G. Read the text and choose the correct answers.
sections.passage:
When I was a student, I wanted to be a detective. Instead, I became a teacher — but crime is still part of my job. Every year I organise a ‘murder mystery’ evening for my class.

Before the evening, each student gets a card with a secret: who they are, where they were at 9 p.m., and one lie they must tell. During the evening, they ask each other questions and try to find the ‘murderer’. Nobody is really hurt, of course!

The first time, I was nervous that the students would be bored. In fact, they loved it, especially the moment at the end when the murderer is revealed. The quiet students often become the best detectives because they listen carefully.

Now other teachers in my school use the idea. If you try it, my advice is simple: keep the rules short and let the students do the talking.

items.q: What did the writer want to be as a student?
What does each student get before the evening?
Which part do students enjoy most?
o: The end, when the murderer is revealed

items.q: Why are quiet students often good detectives?
o: They ask a lot of questions.
